name: Neuronal Intranuclear Inclusion Disease

ethnicAssociations: East Asian populations (notably Japanese and Chinese)

criteria.description: Progressive cognitive decline and motor dysfunction including ataxia and parkinsonism
Presence of eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions in skin biopsy samples
Characteristic high-intensity signals along the corticomedullary junction on diffusion-weighted MRI
Detection of GGC repeat expansion in the NOTCH2NLC gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive neurological symptoms plus either positive skin biopsy or characteristic MRI findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is supportive but not mandatory for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions in skin biopsy
High-intensity signals along corticomedullary junction on DWI MRI

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions positive for ubiquitin and p62
imaging: Diffusion-weighted MRI showing high-intensity signals along the corticomedullary junction
Brain MRI demonstrating cerebral and cerebellar atrophy
genetic: GGC repeat expansion in the NOTCH2NLC gene
other: Electron microscopy revealing filamentous intranuclear inclusions in neurons

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of intranuclear inclusions on skin biopsy
Different MRI patterns without corticomedullary junction hyperintensity
More prominent autonomic failure early in disease
Tremor and ataxia with different MRI findings

redFlags: Rapidly progressive dementia with motor decline
Positive skin biopsy for intranuclear inclusions
references: Sone J, et al. Neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease: a new perspective on an old disease. Neurology. 2016.
Tian Y, et al. Expansion of GGC repeat in NOTCH2NLC is associated with neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease. Nat Genet. 2019.
Fujita K, et al. Clinical and pathological features of neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease. Brain Pathol. 2020.
